name: Glutamates
aliases: E620, E621, E622, E623, E624, E625, glutamate, glutamates, glutamic acid, L-glutamic acid, monosodium glutamate, MSG, sodium glutamate, monopotassium glutamate, potassium glutamate, calcium diglutamate, calcium glutamate, monoammonium glutamate, ammonium glutamate, magnesium diglutamate, magnesium glutamate
what_is: A family of umami flavour enhancers comprising glutamic acid (E620) and its sodium, potassium, calcium, ammonium and magnesium salts (E621–E625). Monosodium glutamate, or MSG, is E621.
why_botia: Glutamate produces the umami taste and already occurs naturally in foods such as ripe tomatoes, Parmesan and soy sauce: the glutamate released by MSG is chemically the same. What became known as “Chinese Restaurant Syndrome” began with a letter published in 1968, not a controlled trial, and controlled studies have not consistently reproduced it under normal eating conditions. JECFA maintains a group ADI “not specified” for E620–E625, while EFSA set a group ADI of 30 mg/kg body weight per day. EFSA derived it from a NOAEL of 3,200 mg MSG/kg body weight per day in a developmental neurotoxicity study, in which higher doses produced neurobehavioural changes, and applied a safety factor of 100.
can_1: Detect E620–E625 and their common names, including monosodium glutamate, MSG and E621.
can_2: Explain the difference between JECFA’s group ADI “not specified” and EFSA’s 30 mg/kg group ADI, including the animal-study NOAEL and safety factor used to derive it.
cannot_1: Determine how much added glutamate is present in a product from the ingredient list alone.
cannot_2: Calculate a person’s total dietary glutamate exposure or predict whether an individual will experience symptoms from the presence of one declared glutamate additive.
